input.quote: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 matches our preferred position: mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and uncapped Excluded Claims for confidentiality, data-protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, with Customer's payment obligation excluded from the cap. "Fees" (§1.5) is a real revenue base, so the cap is not illusory.

input.quote: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Vendor gives a full IP indemnity plus indemnities for breach of law, bodily injury/property damage, Customer Data breaches and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, with standard procedure (§20.4) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies (§20.5); Customer's indemnity is narrowly limited to its own material and unlawful use. Indemnities also sit outside the liability cap as Excluded Claims, so no super-cap is needed.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory.
input.rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds us; Section 12.3 expressly confirms our freedom to develop, acquire, sell and operate in any field or territory. (The exclusivity and non-solicit clauses in §2.2 and §12.4 are addressed under their own rules.)

input.quote: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: This is exclusive dealing for the entire three-year term with no performance-based exit, which is walk-away territory and also contradicts Section 12.3. We propose deleting it; if protection is needed, we could accept exclusivity for a defined category for 12 months ending automatically on missed service levels.

input.quote: Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: This is an open-ended MFN burdening us in favour of the Vendor across all technology suppliers, with no product limit, time limit or comparison carve-outs. We propose deletion; MFN pricing granted to us would be welcome.

input.quote: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
input.rationale: The restriction is one-way, runs 18 months post-termination, covers every person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, includes a no-hire ("engage") element and has no general-advertising carve-out, so it fails the fallback. We have narrowed it to a mutual 12-month non-solicit for personnel involved in the Services with the usual carve-outs.

input.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only cause-based termination (breach, insolvency, security/service failures) and the term is three years, so we have no convenience exit — a deviation. We have inserted a new §9.4 allowing Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees; Vendor has no convenience right, which is correct.

input.quote: Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
input.rationale: The 180-day non-renewal window exceeds our 90-day walk-away threshold and well exceeds the 60-day fallback; we have shortened it to 30 days. The 12-month renewal term and the CPI/3% uplift cap with 90 days' notice in §8.3 already meet our position (only the 60-day Vendor reminder is absent, which we simply note).

input.quote: This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
input.rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County is our preferred position; there is no arbitration clause.

input.quote: Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Preferred position met: we may assign freely to Affiliates and successors, Vendor needs our consent (including on change of control) and may never assign to a competitor, and §24.4 confirms our change of control gives Vendor no termination, repricing or suspension right.

input.quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
input.rationale: We own Customer Data and our pre-existing IP (§14.1), we own and receive an assignment of Deliverables (§14.2), Vendor Technology stays with Vendor but is covered by the perpetual §13.2 licence (§14.3), and no joint ownership is created (§14.4). No Customer IP or data is assigned to Vendor.

input.quote: Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer.
input.rationale: Preferred position met: Affiliates and contractors are covered without notice conditions, paid-up/embedded licences are perpetual and irrevocable (§13.2), licences are transferable to Affiliates and successors, and revocation is limited to material uncured breach after notice and cure (§13.3).

input.quote: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
input.rationale: Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems is expressly walk-away territory and also conflicts with §22.2's no-direct-access language. We have limited audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice by an independent auditor with no system access; the §22.2 cost allocation (Vendor pays unless underpayment exceeds 5%) already meets our position.

input.quote: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: This is an uncapped daily penalty payable by us triggered by any delay in a dependency, however minor — outside even the fallback (a 3-month early-termination fee). We propose deletion; Vendor's remedy for our delay should be schedule relief.

input.quote: For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
input.rationale: Vendor warrants professional and workmanlike performance, 90-day Deliverable conformance (and hosted Services conformance for the whole term), compliance with law and no malicious code, with re-perform/repair/replace/refund remedies (§19.4), and §19.5 confirms the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties.

input.quote: Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.
input.rationale: Section 18 matches our preferred limits (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' compensation) for the term plus one year, with certificates on request and confirmation that insurance does not limit liability.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: Preferred position met: no minimum commitment, take-or-pay or shortfall exposure, and §7.1 bars unstated minimum-use charges.

input.quote: Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form.
input.rationale: Section 11 meets the preferred position: up to six months' transition assistance, return of Customer Data within 30 days in a machine-readable format (with no fee-dispute hostage right), and certified deletion thereafter.
